comments.content: The gate is released here on defaults while the appearance fields still hold `MainState` defaults, and the `combine` collector is **not** cancelled. So if the persistence read finishes just after the 2s watchdog (e.g. slow cold-start DataStore), the app's first frame renders with default personality/paper/accent/dark+amoled, and only once the combine emits does the UI re-theme — a visible flash. Combined with the `catch` below, `isAppearanceLoaded` now has three writers with different semantics (two of which set the flag without the values), which contradicts the "sole writer" comment above. This may be acceptable as a last-resort degradation, but please confirm the flash is intended; if not, the fallback should avoid opening the gate before the first snapshot lands (or apply the snapshot atomically so it can never be observed half-applied).

comments.content: The KDoc promises "Errors are logged; silent degradation would hide real breakage", but the most likely startup failure — the flow not producing a value in time — is swallowed completely silently: `withTimeoutOrNull` *returns* `null` instead of throwing, so the `catch` is never entered and nothing is logged. For nullable flows (`getAppLanguage(): Flow<String?>`) the timed-out result is also indistinguishable from a legitimate `null` value. Suggest using `withTimeout` and catching `TimeoutCancellationException` explicitly so the timeout is observable (requires `import kotlinx.coroutines.TimeoutCancellationException` and `import kotlinx.coroutines.withTimeout`).

On this failure path the gate is released, but `firstEmitted` is never completed, so the watchdog child coroutine stays parked inside `withTimeoutOrNull` for the full 2 s and then emits a misleading `"Appearance preference load timed out, releasing gate on defaults"` warning (plus a redundant flag write) even though the real cause was the exception logged just above. Either cancel the watchdog job or complete the deferred here so the watchdog cannot report a timeout that never happened.

The ViewModel is resolved with Koin's eager `getViewModel()` (unlike `by viewModels()`, which is lazy) while `onCreate` is still *before* `super.onCreate(savedInstanceState)`. Obtaining the ViewModel immediately touches the activity's `ViewModelStore`, which androidx's `ComponentActivity` only supports once the activity is attached (`"You can't call ViewModelStore before onCreate()"`), and the official splash-screen pattern calls `super.onCreate()` right after `installSplashScreen()` and wires the condition afterwards. Please call `super.onCreate(savedInstanceState)` immediately after `installSplashScreen()` and move the ViewModel lookup/condition wiring below it — the condition is still set well before the first draw, so the splash behaviour is unchanged.
